response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.SEX, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.SEX), t AS (SELECT SUM(n) * 1.0 AS total, AVG(n * 1.0) AS avg_n FROM c) SELECT c.SEX, c.n AS test_records, c.n * 1.0 / t.total AS share_of_total, c.n - t.avg_n AS above_average FROM c CROSS JOIN t WHERE c.n > t.avg_n ORDER BY c.n DESC

assumptions.assumption: Only Laboratory rows whose ID matches a Patient row are counted (inner join). The average per sex is total matched records divided by the number of distinct SEX groups. Share of total is a fraction from 0 to 1, not a percentage.
Patients with a NULL or empty SEX value form their own group. That group counts toward the number of sexes, so it affects the average.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude patients with NULL or empty SEX, so the average and total cover only recorded sexes.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.SEX, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(p.SEX) <> '' GROUP BY p.SEX), t AS (SELECT SUM(n) * 1.0 AS total, AVG(n * 1.0) AS avg_n FROM c) SELECT c.SEX, c.n AS test_records, c.n * 1.0 / t.total AS share_of_total, c.n - t.avg_n AS above_average FROM c CROSS JOIN t WHERE c.n > t.avg_n ORDER BY c.n DESC
